item.title: Three Decades of Socioeconomic Inequality in India's Breastfeeding Indicators, 1993-2021
item.description: Although existing literature heavily focuses on the health outcomes of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) in India, studies addressing socioeconomic inequalities across a broad spectrum of breastfeeding indicators remain scarce. We utilized five waves of National Family Health Survey data (1993-2021) to analyze temporal trends and socioeconomic inequalities, proxied by maternal education (no formal schooling, 1st-5th grade, 6th-8th grade, 9th-12th grade, and above 12th grade) and household wealth...

item.title: Functionally declining microbiota in chronic disease: beyond taxonomic loss
item.description: Microbiota deterioration in modern human populations has been linked to chronic disease, and taxonomic profiling is increasingly used to understand, diagnose, and guide treatment. Yet such profiles do not fully capture disease-relevant microbiota states. I propose functional decline within retained taxa as a distinct axis of microbiota deterioration, complementary to taxonomic loss. Modern environmental pressures can drive not only taxonomic loss but also directional selection toward variants or...

item.title: CO<sub>2</sub> Capture in MOFs: Connecting Experiments, Multiscale Simulations, and Data-Driven Approaches
item.description: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous materials for CO(2) capture due to their tunable pore structures and chemically versatile adsorption sites. However, achieving efficient capture at low CO(2) concentrations while balancing adsorption strength, regeneration, and structural stability remains challenging. Existing reviews often treat experimental and computational investigations separately, limiting the development of unified design principles. This review integrates...

item.title: Transitional Nursing Care for Oesophageal Cancer Patients: A Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with oesophageal cancer require multifaceted, continuous transitional nursing care across the care continuum, yet current interventions inadequately address relational, social, and system-level needs. Evidence gaps exist between patients' experienced needs and available interventions, particularly in hospital-to-community care coordination and nonsurgical treatment pathways.

item.title: Modeling Logical Interdependencies: Quantifying Systemic Risk From Rule-Governed Actions
item.description: Systemic risk in critical infrastructure is often analyzed through physical, geographic, and cyber interdependencies. Yet infrastructures are also interdependent through the governing rules that organize human action. These rule-mediated connections are a form of logical interdependency, and breakdowns in rule-governed action can create pathways through which disruption spreads. This paper develops a framework for diagnosing and quantifying this underrecognized source of systemic risk. It does...

item.title: Pepper RING-type E3 ligase, CaANKR1, negatively regulates drought tolerance by modulating CaMAPK1 stability
item.description: Drought stress severely restricts plant growth and productivity, and abscisic acid (ABA)-mediated signaling plays a central role in coordinating adaptive responses to water deficit. Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are widely involved in plant stress signaling; however, the ubiquitin-mediated regulation of MAPK stability during drought responses remains poorly understood. In this study, we conducted a yeast two-hybrid screening and identified CaMAPK1, a pepper (Capsicum annuum)...

item.title: The effects of intravenous glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with improved survival or overall infection rates in critically ill adults. Current evidence does not support routine IV glutamine supplementation in unselected critically ill patients.

item.description: Understanding the interfacial layer (IFL) between hydraulic calcium silicate cements (CSCs) and root dentine is essential for optimising CSC performance and developing next-generation biomaterials. This scholarly review summarises current evidence on IFL composition, formation, structure, and clinical significance. item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite universal health insurance, regional disparities in access to retinal surgery persist in Korea, with services concentrated in the Seoul metropolitan area. Transfer was independently associated with visual disability but not reoperation. The underlying mechanism likely involves referral of complex cases, patient preference, and transfer-related delay, although claims data cannot distinguish their relative contributions. item.description: CONCLUSION: Compared with CC, Epi-Rx may be associated with improved survival outcomes in R/R PTCL. Prospective comparative studies are warranted to confirm this finding.

item.description: Acute neurobehavioral deterioration during carotid artery stenting (CAS) requires prompt evaluation for serious neurological complications. We report a patient in their 70s who developed profound hyperactive delirium approximately 15 minutes after receiving prophylactic intravenous atropine (0.25 mg) during CAS. item.description: CONCLUSION: These divergent findings raise the possibility that elevated circulating CCL2 levels in sarcopenia reflect a compensatory response to muscle deterioration rather than a direct pathogenic driver, highlighting the need for further mechanistic validation.

item.description: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with systemic metabolic dysregulation; however, the molecular pathways linking metabolic signaling to skin inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify cannabinoid 1 receptor (CB1R) in macrophages as a key immunometabolic regulator of psoriatic inflammation and a potential therapeutic target. item.description: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. item.title: Microbubble Timing and Vascular Geometry Are Associated With Vessel-Level Blood-Brain Barrier Opening During Focused Ultrasound
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Microbubble handling and injection-to-sonication timing are potential protocol variables in FUS-BBBO studies. Control-normalized extravascular metrics provide a reproducible framework for vessel-level longitudinal 2-photon quantification.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Nurses and hospital staff expressed a cautiously positive stance toward the utilisation of robots in the context of hospital nursing care. However, there are concerns regarding the impact of robots on the fundamental responsibilities of nursing, particularly with regard to patient interaction, emotional support, and the potential loss of the human aspect of care. item.description: Balancing the acquisition of the macronutrients nitrogen (N) and potassium (K) is critical for plant growth, yet the mechanisms that balance N and K acquisition remain poorly understood. item.description: Cobalt (Co) complexes of porphyrin derivatives possess distinctive redox properties, and hence, their development has attracted significant interest across a wide range of fields. Herein, we report the new examples of the Co complexes of 5,15-diazaporphyrin (DAP) and 5-monoazaporphyrin (MAP) derivatives bearing meso-aryl groups. item.description: Long term xenografts often fail in association with evidence of coagulation pathway dysregulation, which may be caused in part by the inefficient binding of inactivated protein C (PC) to porcine thrombomodulin (TBM). This study evaluates the effect of human TBM (hTBM) expression by genetically modified pig endothelium on human platelet activation, adhesion, and aggregation within a dynamic in vitro xenoperfusion model. item.description: The first 1000 days of life are a critical period for establishing lifelong health and development. Breastfeeding, as part of the Nurturing Care Framework, provides unique immunological, nutritional, and psychosocial benefits, while also contributing to the prevention of obesity, diabetes, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs). item.description: Myeloid cell leukemia 1 (MCL-1) is a canonical anti-apoptotic protein crucial for early neurodevelopment. Loss of MCL-1 results in embryonic-lethal neurodevelopmental defects that cannot be rescued by other anti-apoptotic proteins of the B cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) family. Here, we pharmacologically inhibit MCL-1 in human neural progenitor cells and find non-apoptotic roles for MCL-1 in sustaining mitochondrial cristae integrity, fatty acid oxidation and neural progenitor identity. item.description: Ergothioneine (EGT), a micromolecular derivative of histidine containing sulfur, is found in various organisms, including humans. It demonstrates antioxidant properties, reduces inflammation, and potentially possesses antiaging effects for neurodegenerative conditions, positioning EGT as a potential candidate for health enhancement and healthy aging. EGT appears to offer strong protective properties at the cellular level and shows decreased concentration levels in blood plasma in different...

item.description: Covering: 1966 to 2026γ-Amino acids are structurally diverse non-proteinogenic building blocks that endow bacterial natural products with unique conformational, physicochemical, and biological properties. item.title: Development and validation of semi-quantitative FFQ according to Türkiye Dietary Guideline
item.description: CONCLUSION: In summary, the TDG-SFFQ is a potentially valid and reliable tool for evaluating dietary intake in the Turkish adult population.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The salivary cortisol diurnal cycle appears to be a powerful tool for the diagnosis of CS and for the challenging differential diagnosis of non-neoplastic hypercortisolism, with the major advantage of being accessible in ambulatory patients.

item.title: Initial treatment strategies and outcomes across haemodynamic thresholds and risk stratification in incident systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a EUSTAR analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Initial treatment strategies reflected haemodynamic severity and baseline risk, while variation suggested potential implementation gaps. Sustained initial therapy was associated with lower risks of mortality and PAH progression. Contrasting ITT and AT estimates highlight challenges in observational treatment-outcome comparisons. Findings in the milder haemodynamic subgroup support dedicated prospective studies.

item.title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences
item.description: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. item.description: The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified durability demands on rubber hoses used for battery thermal management and coolant circulation, where para-aramid (p-aramid) fibers serve as the reinforcement of choice owing to their high strength, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The use of ICIs in patients with NSCLC and IP produces long-term responses in some cases; however, there is a high possibility of ICI-related pneumonitis. In cases where the condition worsens, post-treatment may be difficult, and the prognosis may be poor.

item.title: A Genetic Risk Approach to Differential Diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes and Risk Stratification in the Spanish Population
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: T1D-GRS2 discriminates T1D from other diabetes etiologies, providing a complementary tool to support diagnostic accuracy. The higher genetic risk associated with a younger age at onset provides key insights for early-stage T1D screening and intervention strategies.

item.title: Single Jaundice in Cirrhosis: A Neglected Acute Decompensation of Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure and Mortality
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhotic inpatients with single jaundice show comparably high short-term mortality and ACLF risk to those with classical AD. Single jaundice shall be considered as an AD event and is predominantly triggered by intrahepatic insults, warranting surveillance equivalent to classical AD and prioritized management of the precipitants.

item.description: CONCLUSION: We developed a promising tool for identifying infants at increased risk of neurodevelopmental delay in low-resource settings, which could help prioritize children for follow-up and specialized interventions.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center Chinese emergency ICU cohort, UCSD-Mayo showed the highest observed discrimination, but improvements were modest and were not uniform across all outcomes, metrics, or decision thresholds. These scores may support risk awareness and monitoring but should not be used as stand-alone treatment rules.

item.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive stage of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease, for which effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings are consistent with a serial indirect pathway in which perceived organizational support is associated with nurses' pressure injury care behaviors through self-efficacy and change fatigue. Longitudinal studies are needed to confirm this pathway.

item.description: Reversing the destructive remodeling of the bone marrow microenvironment during aging remains a major challenge. item.title: Amplification of circularly polarised luminescence through the self-assembly of chiral tri-europium(III) clusters in a polar crystal
item.description: Chiral {Eu^(III)(3)} coordination clusters based on bridging enantiopure 1,1'-binaphthyl-2,2'-diyl phosphato and chlorido ligands are reported. They form polar crystals that exhibit circularly polarised luminescence with a |g(lum)| factor of up to 0.091 at 593 nm, revealing ca. 5-fold enhancement of this chiro-optical effect in comparison to the unassembled Eu(III) complexes in solution.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We identified 20 genetic loci shared between the S-PMD and MPDs, implicating calcium transmission in the pathogenesis of PMDs. Together with the drug enrichment results, this provides a biological basis for repurposing existing drugs in the treatment of PMD.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: With psychometric validation underway, the TGI-3S offers an anamnesis-embedded, brief, yet comprehensive tool for facilitating the assessment of somatic health in patients with mental disorders.

item.description: Escitalopram is a frequently prescribed antidepressant drug. CYP2C19 genotype is a major determinant of escitalopram metabolism and treatment outcome. item.title: Restricted mean survival time ratio in oncology cost-effectiveness analysis: stability and data-driven support for treatment-effect waning modeling and survival extrapolation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Reliance on current HR-based TEW modeling practices alone may be insufficient to fully characterize long-term treatment-effect uncertainty. RMSTR was consistently less dispersed than HR and predictable from early trial data, providing an anchor for extrapolation model selection and TEW uncertainty analysis in oncology economic evaluations.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The LAMP-orpH assay offers a rapid, sensitive, and specific tool for early leptospirosis diagnosis. Its simple colorimetric readout and minimal equipment requirements make it ideal for use in rural and resource-limited settings, providing a practical alternative to MAT, conventional PCR, and qPCR.

This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.
